How plan items and work-items work today"},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-26T15:22:11.695Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_f5918e3b-dfa2-4830-a99f-e46c4e0073f8"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_f5918e3b-dfa2-4830-a99f-e46c4e0073f8:counts:4","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_f5918e3b-dfa2-4830-a99f-e46c4e0073f8","part":4,"quote":"- A **plan item** (e.g. P-521) is a line in a plan: what must be done, plus `blocked-by` edges to other plan items.\n- A **work-item** (e.g. WI-2144482) is the unit an agent claims and works on. Starting a plan creates one work-item per plan item. Later, more work-items can attach to the same plan item (P-521 has 3), and work-items can have child work-items (P-521's have 24 between them)."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-26T15:22:11.695Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_f5918e3b-dfa2-4830-a99f-e46c4e0073f8"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_f5918e3b-dfa2-4830-a99f-e46c4e0073f8:counts:5","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_f5918e3b-dfa2-4830-a99f-e46c4e0073f8","part":5,"quote":"Blocking lives in **three separate stores**:\n1. plan-item `blocked-by` edges;\n2. work-item-to-work-item `blocks` links;\n3. non-work blockers on work-items (events, gates, human decisions) via `work_items:set_blocker`."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-26T15:22:11.695Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_f5918e3b-dfa2-4830-a99f-e46c4e0073f8"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_f5918e3b-dfa2-4830-a99f-e46c4e0073f8:counts:6","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_f5918e3b-dfa2-4830-a99f-e46c4e0073f8","part":6,"quote":"**Sync rules copy state between the two levels** (`plan-items/reflect-rules.ts`, `reconcile-linked-work-items.ts`, `lane-sync-rule.ts`):\n- When a work-item finishes, its plan item is marked done.\n- When a plan item is marked done, its other work-items are closed, **but only if they show no progress** (a safety guard). That is why P-203 and P-204 read done while their work-items read blocked.\n- When a plan item is blocked, its work-items are parked with a \"lane blocked\" gate. This happens immediately when a `blocked-by` edge is edited; any other change waits for a **15-minute sweep**.\n- Nothing flows the other way for work-item `blocks` links or child work-items. The plan cannot see that P-521's real work is stuck on a child."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-26T15:22:11.695Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_f5918e3b-dfa2-4830-a99f-e46c4e0073f8"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_f5918e3b-dfa2-4830-a99f-e46c4e0073f8:counts:7","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_f5918e3b-dfa2-4830-a99f-e46c4e0073f8","part":7,"quote":"## 3. Improvement: one graph"},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-26T15:22:11.695Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_f5918e3b-dfa2-4830-a99f-e46c4e0073f8"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_f5918e3b-dfa2-4830-a99f-e46c4e0073f8:counts:8","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_f5918e3b-dfa2-4830-a99f-e46c4e0073f8","part":8,"quote":"- **A plan item becomes the top-level work-item for its plan line.** The plan is the ordered list of those nodes, which keep their plan fields (phase, importance, decision links). The work under a plan line is its children.\n- **One edge store** holds every dependency and blocker, including holds. `blocked-by` on the plan *is* the work-item `blocks` edge, not a copy of it.\n- **A plan item's status is computed** from its node and children: done when they are done, blocked while any active blocker or hold applies. It is never stored.\n- **The three sync rules and the 15-minute sweep are deleted**, not repaired, because there is nothing left to copy.\n- The plan view, `get_next` and the leader's claimable view all read the same graph, so they cannot disagree."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-26T15:22:11.695Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_f5918e3b-dfa2-4830-a99f-e46c4e0073f8"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_fb75dfba-f9e6-4d17-91c9-d9d3d22acd77","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"correction":{"status":"known","value":{"ref":"report:rpt_fb75dfba-f9e6-4d17-91c9-d9d3d22acd77","supersedes":null,"summary":"","publishedAt":"2026-10-26T14:29:41.361Z","supersededBy":[]},"source":"report_library In 4 hours they were SIGKILLed **15 times**:\n   - 13 times by the memory watchdog for crossing 3,200 MB;\n   - twice by the event-loop sentinel after a 24-second freeze."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-26T12:56:28.786Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_4d75d19c-961c-4227-8455-a2cc24de5975"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_4d75d19c-961c-4227-8455-a2cc24de5975:counts:4","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_4d75d19c-961c-4227-8455-a2cc24de5975","part":4,"quote":"   Each kill dropped every MCP and sync connection on that worker, which is the **reconnecting**. Before each kill, the overloaded worker turned calls away with `429 loop_pressure_critical` and the proxy retried them, which is the **slowness**.\n2. **What filled the workers:** every `coord:inbox` / inbox read without a start time decoded the **newest 25,000 coord messages**, 99.8% of which are broadcasts. There are **182,416 broadcast messages** in the 30-day retention window, arriving at 4,000–12,000 a day. Most come from `system-watchdog` severe-event alarm and resolution traffic sent to every agent. The heap profiler's top live site was **814 MB in the Postgres JSON decoder**.\n3. **Why it wasn't already fixed:** :3070 runs build `d740fc3802` from **10-02**, which is **11,863 commits behind staging**. Staging already pages `coord:inbox` and carries earlier fixes for this exact worker churn. Nothing has reached :3070 because the release gate has been red for about 578 hours (WI-1000605"},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-26T12:56:28.786Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_4d75d19c-961c-4227-8455-a2cc24de5975"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_4d75d19c-961c-4227-8455-a2cc24de5975:counts:5","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_4d75d19c-961c-4227-8455-a2cc24de5975","part":5,"quote":"5, owned by another agent)."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-26T12:56:28.786Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_4d75d19c-961c-4227-8455-a2cc24de5975"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_4d75d19c-961c-4227-8455-a2cc24de5975:counts:6","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_4d75d19c-961c-4227-8455-a2cc24de5975","part":6,"quote":"## What I changed\n- **Temporary mitigation, live now:** raised :3070 from 6 to 9 request workers (`55-memory-envelope.conf`) and restarted at 12:40Z. That stays inside the documented 48 GB memory envelope (worst case 41 GB; actual use was 14 GB, with 108 GB free on the host). Result so far: **0 kills, 0 load-shedding, 0 upstream errors**, and workers at 1.5–2.0 GB. This should go back to 6 once :3070 runs current code.\n- **Durable fix, on staging:** inbox reads now include broadcast messages only from the last 24 hours. Directed mail keeps its full history. It's applied in SQL (so old broadcasts are never loaded) and in a JS filter on all three read paths.\n  - Tests: 6 new regression tests, 22/22 pass.\n  - Typecheck: clean.\n  - Mutation probe: removing the filter is caught.\n  - Takes effect on :3070 when the gate promotes.\n- **Woke the agents this stopped:** 43 parked sessions holding claimed work.\n  - 25 took a turn immediately.\n  - 5 received the wake in their inbox.\n  - 13 are queue"},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-26T12:56:28.786Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_4d75d19c-961c-4227-8455-a2cc24de5975"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_4d75d19c-961c-4227-8455-a2cc24de5975:counts:7","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_4d75d19c-961c-4227-8455-a2cc24de5975","part":7,"quote":"d by the host and will be retried automatically."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-26T12:56:28.786Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_4d75d19c-961c-4227-8455-a2cc24de5975"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_4d75d19c-961c-4227-8455-a2cc24de5975:counts:8","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_4d75d19c-961c-4227-8455-a2cc24de5975","part":8,"quote":"## Filed (not fixed tonight)\n- **EI-27046565771451366:** `system-watchdog` broadcasts severe events to every agent at 4,000–12,000 a day. They reset between **11:08 and 11:14Z**. The one account with usage credits, **aviynw_codex**, has had a **dead login since about 00:12Z**: OpenAI rejects its refresh token with \"Your session has ended. Please log in again.\" The gateway only logged this, about 1,000 times, and told nobody. That left aviynw6_codex (and the codex-cli bridge) carrying the whole fleet."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-26T11:34:17.181Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02:counts:4","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02","part":4,"quote":"2. **A gateway bug turned the shortage into dead sessions.** About 95% of the 429s came from the gateway itself, not from OpenAI. When no account could take a request in time (the gateway's pacing \"shed\"), it answered `429` with **`retry-after: 1`** and **recorded no stall**. The Codex CLI spent its 4–5 retries in a few seconds and quit with \"exceeded retry limit\". Because no stall was recorded, the system that resumes stalled agents had nothing in its queue. Sessions stayed stopped."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-26T11:34:17.181Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02:counts:5","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02","part":5,"quote":"## How it regressed after the earlier fix\nAn earlier fix for this exact error message covered only the path where **OpenAI** returns the 429. That path sends a sensible retry-after based on when the pool recovers, adds the retries-exhausted and pool-recovery headers, and records a stall so the agent is woken later."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-26T11:34:17.181Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02:counts:6","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02","part":6,"quote":"Yesterday's fix for the 4-minute admission waits (commit `9a9fa87645`, 2026-10-25 18:32Z) added a **second** 429 path, where the gateway itself sheds the request. That new path skipped all three steps. Nothing checked that every 429 path behaves the same way, so the gap went unnoticed until today's capacity loss sent most traffic down the new path."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-26T11:34:17.181Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02:counts:7","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02","part":7,"quote":"```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n  A[Codex request] --> B{account free in time?}\n  B -- no, gateway sheds --> C[\"before: 429, retry-after 1, no stall\"]\n  C --> D[CLI retries burn in seconds, session dies, nobody wakes it]\n  B -- no, gateway sheds --> E[\"now: 429, pool-horizon retry-after, exhausted and recovery headers, stall recorded\"]\n  E --> F[stall-waker resumes the session when capacity returns]\n```"},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-26T11:34:17.181Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02:counts:8","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02","part":8,"quote":"**Fix 1: gateway-shed 429s now behave like upstream 429s.** In `packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway/gateway.ts`, both Codex lanes (OAuth and bearer) now build their shed response through one shared helper, `codexLocalShedHeaders`. It records the stall, sets retry-after from the pool's recovery time (capped at 60s, never 1s), and adds the same exhausted and recovery headers as the upstream path.\n- Live since the gateway restart at 07:58:43Z: **46 Codex sheds produced 46 stall records** (10 agents). Before the fix there were none."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-26T11:34:17.181Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02:counts:9","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02","part":9,"quote":"**Fix 2: a dead Codex login now alerts loudly.** Codex refresh rejections and unusable codex-cli logins now raise the same deduplicated blocker escalation and fleet broadcast the Claude dead-credential path already used. It fires once per account until that account works again (or every 6h at most).\n- Live since the restart at 08:14:32Z: escalation `mvoze3ep-0000-5d42b03bc3044ea6acf19e3bb90bb802` opened at 08:14:54Z for aviynw_codex."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-26T11:34:17.181Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02:counts:10","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02","part":10,"quote":"## Guards against a repeat\nAll guards live in `packages/operator-core/lib/inference-gateway/gateway-codex-local-shed.test.ts`, 5 of 5 passing:\n- **Behaviour, both lanes:** a gateway shed must return 429 with retry-after between 1s (exclusive) and 60s, the exhausted and pool-recovery headers, and exactly one new stall record.\n- **Structural:** no literal `'retry-after': '1'` anywhere in `gateway.ts`, and every Codex shed-429 site must go through `codexLocalShedHeaders`. A future third shed path that skips it fails the build. This is the guard that would have caught yesterday's regression.\n- **Credential death, behaviour:** a refresh rejected with `refresh_token_invalidated` fires the alert exactly once.\n- **Credential death, structural:** every Codex credential-rejection log line must also fire the alert.\n- **Proof the guards can fail:** three mutation probes with `scripts/mutation-probe.sh`, each one **caught**: removing the stall record, capping retry-after back to 1s, and silencing t"},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-26T11:34:17.181Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02:counts:11","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02","part":11,"quote":"he credential alert.\n- Neighbouring suites pass (`gateway.test.ts`, `codex-oauth-kernel-adapter.test.ts`, `gateway-account-rate-pacing.test.ts`). The typecheck over all changed files is clean."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-26T11:34:17.181Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02:counts:12","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_f3fa941c-bd61-49d1-a8fc-3cd29beaab02","part":12,"quote":"## Waiting on you, Avi\n- **Re-login the dead Codex credential.** Run `codex login` as **aviynw@gmail.com** into CODEX_HOME `~/.papercusp-workspaces/papercusp-workspace/.papercusp/deploy-credentials/aviynw_codex.codex-cli`. It has had 10 reds since, and its latest verdict is 5 days stale.\n- All 22 ship-readiness readings I took were answered by that build.\n- Direct effect: **9 of the 22 plans fail with `rubric_unresolved`.** Their acceptance rubric exists, but the old build can't read a rubric written by newer code. These plans cannot ship until `:3070` is updated, whatever their authors do.\n  - This is already filed as WI-9999934. Packaging means rebuilding each platform as a provider package (providerAdapter { describe, syncPage, invoke }, network only via host.fetch + egressHosts, auth via oauth/clientRegistrationRef or setup.credentials). The per-platform normalization functions and their tests are ported. Reconcile loops are replaced by syncPage. Per-adapter retry/backoff (redditRetryDelayMs, youtubeRetryDelayMs, tiktokRetryDelayMs and the Bluesky and Mastodon variants), the ~14 per-platform error classes, social-egress.ts, and cursor-expiry backfill triggering are deleted: the host runtime already owns them (connector-runtime.ts header: retryAfterSeconds backoff, cursor reset on cursor-expired, lease, version-scoped dedupe). D-012 — Keep resource-token exchanges in the existing host credential path\nDate: 2026-10-14\n[self-imposed implementation decision for D-003/D-004] Measured: 2026-10-14, packages/operator-core/lib/integrations/host-fetch.ts:createHostFetch rejects caller Authorization and injects the source's account token; packages/plugin-sdk/src/provider.ts:ProviderOAuthDescriptor supports account identity but no resource-token exchange. Meta Pages needs a user-to-Page credential hop (P-027) and Instagram uses the same Page grant. Extend the existing OAuth descriptor with resourceToken: an HTTPS collection endpoint, source-config resource selector, token field, optional required resource permissions and bounded same-endpoint pagination. The Discord Gateway also needs (a) GET https://discord.com/api/v10/gateway/bot with `Authorization: Bot <token>`, with `?v=10&encoding=json` added to the returned URL, (b) IDENTIFY (op 2) carrying the bot token inside a socket frame after HELLO (op 10), (c) heartbeats (op 1, d = last sequence `s`) every `d.heartbeat_interval` ms, plus an immediate one when the gateway sends op 1, and (d) only DISPATCH frames (op 0) are data. Discord has ONE bot token for the gateway and REST, while Slack has separate app and bot tokens."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-22T09:06:35.439Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_c6133255-5944-4504-93e8-99b23a730091"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_c6133255-5944-4504-93e8-99b23a730091:counts:160","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_c6133255-5944-4504-93e8-99b23a730091","part":160,"quote":"Decision:\n(1) SDK ProviderSocketIngressDescriptor gains optional data, with no provider names: `open.query` (string map appended to the opened socket URL) and `session { hello { match, intervalPath }, identify { frame }, heartbeat { frame, requestMatch? }, sequencePath?, deliver? }`. Frames are JSON objects. A string value that is exactly `{{credential}}` (allowed only in identify.frame) or `{{sequence}}` is substituted by the HOST, so the credential still never reaches provider code. With `deliver` set, only matching envelopes reach ingress.normalize, so protocol frames never do. Validator (provider.ts ingressDescriptorIssues) and papercusp-plugin.schema.json change together.\n(2) The open request's Authorization comes from the ingress credential field's own declared `auth.scheme` (providerCredentialHeaderValue). This is derived, not a new field: Slack's app_token (no auth) stays Bearer and Discord's bot_token (scheme bot) sends `Bot <token>`. An ingress credential may also carry `host"},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-22T09:06:35.439Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_c6133255-5944-4504-93e8-99b23a730091"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_c6133255-5944-4504-93e8-99b23a730091:counts:161","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_c6133255-5944-4504-93e8-99b23a730091","part":161,"quote":"s` (only perPrincipal is refused).\n(3) Heartbeats run from the existing managed reconcile tick (15s). No new timer: a beat is sent when now >= lastBeat + interval - tick, and at once on the gateway's request. The last sequence is read from every envelope. There is no RESUME: each reconnect (op 7 RECONNECT, op 9 INVALID_SESSION, via the existing `reconnect` match) re-identifies, so messages sent during a reconnect gap are not backfilled (disclosed in the package README).\n(4) The discord package goes to 0.2.0. It adds datatype chat-message and capabilities ingress.normalize and chat.reply, with intents GUILDS|GUILD_MESSAGES|DIRECT_MESSAGES|MESSAGE_CONTENT = 37377. MESSAGE_CONTENT is privileged and must be switched on in the Developer Portal. normalize maps MESSAGE_CREATE from non-bot authors (filtered to the source's guildId when set; DMs kept) to chat-message records: nativeId `<channel>:<message>`, payload { id, channelId, threadId = message id, threadKey = message_reference.message_id"},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-22T09:06:35.439Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_c6133255-5944-4504-93e8-99b23a730091"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_c6133255-5944-4504-93e8-99b23a730091:counts:162","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_c6133255-5944-4504-93e8-99b23a730091","part":162,"quote":" or null, sender, text, mentions, extensions.discord }. chat.reply posts to /channels/{channelId}/messages with message_reference { message_id: threadId, fail_if_not_exists:false }, allowed_mentions { parse:[], replied_user:false } and a nonce derived from the idempotency inputs, and returns { channelId, threadId, messageTs: <new message id> }. **A conformance probe per agent.**\n   - First a no-token handshake: `initialize` plus `session/new`, like agentproto's `harness check`.\n   - Then one scripted session that edits a file and runs a command. It records whether those went through `fs/write_text_file` and `terminal/create`, and whether a permission request was raised.\n2. **Trust tiers from the probe result.**\n   - *Enforced* agents may edit the shared tree.\n   - *Advisory* agents are restricted to read-only or scout roles, or an isolation worktree like the migration roles already use, until a fallback guard exists. One possible fallback: compare file changes against the lock ledger and flag violations.\n3. **Re-probe on every agent version bump.** Behaviour can change between releases."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-21T14:35:06.116Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_35581c64-2ca1-4c34-aa9e-296e8b5458c3"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_35581c64-2ca1-4c34-aa9e-296e8b5458c3:counts:7","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_35581c64-2ca1-4c34-aa9e-296e8b5458c3","part":7,"quote":"## Direction 2 — Papercusp as an ACP agent (editors drive Papercusp)"},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-21T14:35:06.116Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_35581c64-2ca1-4c34-aa9e-296e8b5458c3"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_35581c64-2ca1-4c34-aa9e-296e8b5458c3:counts:8","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_35581c64-2ca1-4c34-aa9e-296e8b5458c3","part":8,"quote":"```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n  ED[\"Editor\\n(Zed / JetBrains / Devin Desktop)\"] <-- ACP --> PSU[\"psu acp proxy\\nadds identity, MCP tools,\\npresence, transcript, lock checks\"]\n  PSU <-- ACP --> BE[\"Backend agent\\n(claude-acp, codex-acp, omp, or any registry agent)\"]\n  PSU <--> OP2[\"Papercusp operator\"]\n```"},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-21T14:35:06.116Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_35581c64-2ca1-4c34-aa9e-296e8b5458c3"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_35581c64-2ca1-4c34-aa9e-296e8b5458c3:counts:9","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_35581c64-2ca1-4c34-aa9e-296e8b5458c3","part":9,"quote":"Directions 1 and 2 share one component. A fire of those proves nothing about the condition. Paper: arXiv 2610.14224, \"Harness²: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World\".\n- It improves the harness around a fixed model, never the weights. The harness is a tree of eight editable components: system prompt, guardrails, memory, tool guidance, subagents, skills, scripts and plugins (hooks).\n- **Task-level loop (Propose–Probe–Compose), with no ground truth.** k editors propose \"INV\" edits (how the agent works) and k propose \"DOM\" edits (what a practitioner knows). Each candidate is run on the same task. k composers then read every harness and every trajectory and compose a final harness from the differences in behaviour. The finals are run, and a blind selector picks one output from an anonymised, shuffled pool. Picking the unmodified harness's output is explicitly allowed.\n- **Cross-task loop.** A reflector writes `EXPERIENCE.md` (why this one was picked, what the lesson is). So \"handled\" reads as \"done\".\n3. **The agent marked its own items \"blocked\" without proof.** WI-…14860's blocker text ends \"…this lane has no actionable independent work.\" Nothing checks that claim, and it was false. *[inferred, not verified in code]* A self-declared blocked state may also ma"},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-16T02:15:41.557Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_24408ef5-04d2-45ca-b56a-27ee3cca8c98"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_24408ef5-04d2-45ca-b56a-27ee3cca8c98:counts:7","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_24408ef5-04d2-45ca-b56a-27ee3cca8c98","part":7,"quote":"ke the item look legitimately parked to the sweep.\n4. **The backstop is overwhelmed.** The sweep caps wakes at 5 per pass and one per stop. It was built to catch sessions that go quiet for any cause, including a crashed CLI, a failed respawn or a wedged host. In those cases nothing inside the session is still running to notice, so only an outside sweep can see them. The 5-wake cap exists so that a mass stop, such as a provider usage limit that halts dozens of agents at once, doesn't trigger a thundering herd of wakes."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-16T02:15:41.557Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_24408ef5-04d2-45ca-b56a-27ee3cca8c98"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_24408ef5-04d2-45ca-b56a-27ee3cca8c98:counts:10","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_24408ef5-04d2-45ca-b56a-27ee3cca8c98","part":10,"quote":"1. **Turn-end gate (Claude + Codex, one shared server check).** When AUTO is on, the session holds unfinished work, and `loop:status.rewake.rewakeGuaranteed` is false, the gate blocks the stop once. The reason it gives lists the held items and four ways out: do the next step, arm a wake, release or close the items, or end the loop with an explicit \"I'm going wake-less\" acknowledgement. Both clients support this. Claude uses `decision:block` and the `stop_hook_active` once-only rule. Codex supports `decision:'block'` on Stop per `~/.papercusp/hooks/inject/adapters/codex.mjs`.\n2. **Per-agent timer if it still stops.** The server registers a timeout wake for that session, about 15 minutes with jitter. The wake asks for a decision, not another status check: do the next step, record a real event-backed blocker, or release. Two wakes in a row with no progress end the timer and send you one page. That avoids the \"verification ceremony\" loop you objected to on 2026-09-23.\n3. **Rewrite the inbo"},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-16T02:15:41.557Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_24408ef5-04d2-45ca-b56a-27ee3cca8c98"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_24408ef5-04d2-45ca-b56a-27ee3cca8c98:counts:11","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_24408ef5-04d2-45ca-b56a-27ee3cca8c98","part":11,"quote":"x-wake prompt.** Append the held items, AUTO state and wake status: \"handling this message does not end your lane.\"\n4. **\"Blocked\" must name its wake.** A self-set blocker counts as a reason to rest only if it names an event the agent is awaiting or a re-check time. Otherwise the gate treats the item as still live.\n5. **Measure it.** Make the halt rate a recorded rubric check: of machine-started turns under AUTO while holding work, the share that end with nothing armed to wake the agent. The only real push is the task brief attached when an agent *claims* a work item.\n- Nudging has been measured and it fails: the grep → `lsp:query` advisory fired **138 times in 7 days across 42 sessions and was followed once** (WI-10006282, recorded in the header of `bash-substitution/pairs/code-search.ts`).\n- **Recommendation: stop advising, start answering.** Put the answer into the agent's context at the moment it needs it — at a grep, on first touch of a file, after an interface edit, on a red test, and at completion — served from the precomputed graph snapshot so it's fast, All io2 volumes are now Block Express; on Nitro, AWS specifies average latency below 500 microseconds for 16 KiB operations and volume ceilings of 256,000 IOPS / 4,000 MiB/s. No synthetic resident-memory padding or fake inference was used. Upstream credentials stayed on the controller behind a private loopback SSH forward."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-15T13:25:54.337Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_90562da4-1ea8-4dec-82be-f372cef50d23"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_90562da4-1ea8-4dec-82be-f372cef50d23:counts:7","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_90562da4-1ea8-4dec-82be-f372cef50d23","part":7,"quote":"Google: C4 standard-8, eight vCPUs, 30 GiB RAM, Ubuntu kernel 7.0.0-1014-gcp; 256 GiB Hyperdisk Balanced swap at 16,000 provisioned IOPS / 400 MiB/s. AWS gp3 permits 256 1-GiB volumes at about $20.48 capacity-only, but the nominal per-volume 3,000-IOPS baselines are bounded by EC2 attachment and EBS host limits. AWS io2 requires 4 GiB: 64 4-GiB volumes at the 100-IOPS minimum would cost about $448/month ($32 capacity plus $416 IOPS), versus $38.50 for one 256-GiB volume at 100 IOPS or $422 for one at the tested 6,000 IOPS. Multiple swap devices can spread independent page traffic; they do not stripe each I/O unless a RAID/device-mapper layer is added, which increases failure and operational risk."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not This is materially faster disk-only performance than the measured network disks, but the tested Z3's storage alone cost $240/month and its whole VM/boot configuration about $846.97/month. Host RAM, warmed working set and run order differ, so the cross-host input-echo values are descriptive rather than an isolated SSD comparison. Net saving after a minute: about 10% of their memory with compressed RAM, 15–28% with disk swap.\n- **Disk swap makes waking agents slow.** On `pd-balanced`, the disk type our cloud desktops use, waking 16 agents at once took **39–40 s**, against 1.5 s when they are in RAM.\n- **Compressed RAM (zram) is nearly free and nearly as fast as RAM.** One wake took 0.29 s (RAM: 0.19 s), and 16 at once took 3.0 s. It costs nothing to run.\n- **The fastest disk is Local SSD.** It is a physically attached NVMe drive. It is about **3× faster than `pd-ssd` and 11× faster than `pd-balanced`** at waking a group of agents. It is still slower than zram, and it isn't offered on the `e2` machines our cloud desktops use.\n- **Recommendation:** don't buy disks for swap. Keep stopping idle agent processes (\"parking\"), which frees all of their memory. Replies came from a local stand-in for the model API, so wake times measure only the machine's own cost; real model latency adds the same amount to every option.\n2. **Push all of each agent's memory out to the swap option under test.** About 150 MiB per agent, 3.6–3.8 GiB in total.\n3. **Leave the agents idle for 60 s.** Nothing is typed into them.\n4. **Wake 8 agents one at a time, then the other 16 all at once.** A wake means typing a prompt and timing until the reply is on screen.\n5. **Throughout, check every 0.1 s how long it takes to start a tiny program.** This is the \"does the machine stay responsive\" signal."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-14T08:33:40.747Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_ad53ed14-b22d-4ab6-91f9-da3940e8ad59"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_ad53ed14-b22d-4ab6-91f9-da3940e8ad59:counts:8","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_ad53ed14-b22d-4ab6-91f9-da3940e8ad59","part":8,"quote":"## 2. **The terminals touch most of their memory even when nobody is using them.** Nothing was typed during the idle minute, yet with zram, where reading back is cheap, more than half came back. Counting the 30 s it took to push all 24 out, it was about two-thirds. *(Likely cause: the terminal's JavaScript runtime does housekeeping on a timer, such as garbage collection. That is an inference, not measured.)*\n- **On disks, less came back only because the disk is slower.** The amount follows disk speed, so the agents are trying to reload just as much.\n- **The zram saving shrinks after the first push-out.** At first zram stored agent memory at **4.4× compression** (3.2 GiB in 0.72 GiB of RAM). After the agents pulled most of it back, the zram store still held **473 MiB of RAM for 461 MiB of data**. The leftover space wasn't freed during the test."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-14T08:33:40.747Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_ad53ed14-b22d-4ab6-91f9-da3940e8ad59"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_ad53ed14-b22d-4ab6-91f9-da3940e8ad59:counts:13","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_ad53ed14-b22d-4ab6-91f9-da3940e8ad59","part":13,"quote":"Starting a tiny program took 1–2 ms (median) in every option, so nothing froze."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-14T08:33:40.747Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_ad53ed14-b22d-4ab6-91f9-da3940e8ad59"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_ad53ed14-b22d-4ab6-91f9-da3940e8ad59:counts:14","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_ad53ed14-b22d-4ab6-91f9-da3940e8ad59","part":14,"quote":"The worst moments were brief hitches of **13–75 ms**, during the 16-agent wakes in the *faster* options (RAM, zram, Local SSD, and `pd-ssd` on e2). **Idle terminals use memory, not CPU.** One costs about 175 MiB (memory-controller measure) and almost no CPU. On a 16 GB machine, memory runs out first.\n- **Waking many at once uses CPU.** That is where the responsiveness hitches came from.\n- **Busy agents (tests, typechecks) run out of CPU first**, per earlier measurements (D-041).\n- **The biggest memory users are not the terminals.** They are workspace servers (~3.4 GiB each) and code-intelligence daemons. Those were **not** tested in swap; a follow-up test could check whether they stay out of RAM."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-14T08:33:40.747Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_ad53ed14-b22d-4ab6-91f9-da3940e8ad59"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_ad53ed14-b22d-4ab6-91f9-da3940e8ad59:counts:23","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_ad53ed14-b22d-4ab6-91f9-da3940e8ad59","part":23,"quote":"## 4. It also detects a parent pid that was reused by an unrelated process; pids wrap about daily here. Five new regression tests cover this.\n- **Outside the helper.** The task manager's 30-second reaper has a new **orphaned-sidecar** class. It reads each running helper's declared parent from `/proc`. If that parent is gone, or the pid now belongs to a process that started after the helper, the reaper stops the helper's whole process group. It first gives the helper 60 seconds to shut itself down cleanly. This layer works even if the orphan is wedged and its own watch never fires. 21 new tests and the 60 existing reaper tests pass.\n- **Considered and not used:** a kernel \"kill me when my parent dies\" signal. Helpers are started by worker processes, but their real owner is the main server. With that signal, a routine worker restart would kill health"},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-14T06:51:30.477Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_1b76b06b-4f04-46ba-86d6-e5d438245f08"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_1b76b06b-4f04-46ba-86d6-e5d438245f08:counts:7","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_1b76b06b-4f04-46ba-86d6-e5d438245f08","part":7,"quote":"y helpers. *(design reasoning, not measured)*"},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-14T06:51:30.477Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_1b76b06b-4f04-46ba-86d6-e5d438245f08"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_1b76b06b-4f04-46ba-86d6-e5d438245f08:counts:8","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_1b76b06b-4f04-46ba-86d6-e5d438245f08","part":8,"quote":"**Still open (owned by me):** WI-6554700010012202. The kernel never needed to swap. Busy agents ran out of something else first: the queue for heavy test and typecheck jobs.\n- **Parking beats swapping for idle agents.** A parked Claude agent with no process frees about **215 MB**, and waking it costs about **+0.65 s** (D-025). Swap could only offer part of that, and only if the memory stays untouched.\n- **The open question is the one you asked.** When a swapped-out agent wakes, does it immediately pull all its memory back from disk? Agents run on Node, whose garbage collector walks the whole heap. That is unmeasured, and it is exactly follow-up **WI-10005475** (open, unowned)."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-14T06:51:30.477Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_1b76b06b-4f04-46ba-86d6-e5d438245f08"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_1b76b06b-4f04-46ba-86d6-e5d438245f08:counts:14","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_1b76b06b-4f04-46ba-86d6-e5d438245f08","part":14,"quote":"- **Idle workspaces are memory-bound.** Each workspace server costs ~3.4 GiB, and memory runs out before CPU (D-045).\n- **Busy engineering agents are CPU-bound.** Tests and typechecks run out of CPU first (D-041).\n- **The agent terminals themselves are not the big cost**, at about 110–220 MB each. The heavy items are workspace servers (~3.4 GiB), code-intelligence daemons (~17 GiB each) and big typecheck jobs (up to ~14 GB).\n- **This tower right now is short of both:** CPU ~80% busy and 270 GiB in swap."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-14T06:51:30.477Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_1b76b06b-4f04-46ba-86d6-e5d438245f08"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_1b76b06b-4f04-46ba-86d6-e5d438245f08:counts:15","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_1b76b06b-4f04-46ba-86d6-e5d438245f08","part":15,"quote":"1. Canva's API can export an email design as HTML (`html_bundle` / `html_standalone`). Not confirmed that the MCP connection offers that. Text placed inside images gets flattened, so it's better for graphics than for email layout. |"},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-14T00:38:58.562Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_6c14a624-040c-4a67-8c53-754bd0be6971"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_6c14a624-040c-4a67-8c53-754bd0be6971:counts:8","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_6c14a624-040c-4a67-8c53-754bd0be6971","part":8,"quote":"## 3. Social connectors for marketing Papercusp"},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-14T00:38:58.562Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_6c14a624-040c-4a67-8c53-754bd0be6971"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_6c14a624-040c-4a67-8c53-754bd0be6971:counts:9","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_6c14a624-040c-4a67-8c53-754bd0be6971","part":9,"quote":"| Platform | State |\n|---|---|\n| Bluesky, Mastodon, Reddit, YouTube, Facebook Pages, Instagram, Threads | Read and post connectors built |\n| LinkedIn | Can post only to a personal profile. Company-page posting needs LinkedIn's Community Management API, which LinkedIn must approve. Sign-ins last 60 days and can't be refreshed automatically. |\n| TikTok | Can only send drafts to the TikTok inbox until TikTok audits the app |\n| X | Not built. Parked on your decision about cost, because X charges for API access. |"},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-14T00:38:58.562Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_6c14a624-040c-4a67-8c53-754bd0be6971"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_6c14a624-040c-4a67-8c53-754bd0be6971:counts:10","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_6c14a624-040c-4a67-8c53-754bd0be6971","part":10,"quote":"**Worth adding.** Our audience is developers and people building AI agents.\n- **LinkedIn company page.** Apply for the Community Management API now, because approval takes time.\n- **X.** The biggest developer audience. Needs a decision on paying for the API.\n- **Discord.** The draft plan already covers sending announcements to Discord (P-005). A bot for our own community server would go further.\n- **Developer blogs.** dev.to and Hashnode both have publishing APIs, so agents could cross-post blog posts and docs.\n- **Hacker News and Product Hunt.** Neither lets apps post. Agents can watch for mentions and draft posts; a person submits them.\n- **GitHub releases and discussions.** Already covered by the GitHub packages."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-14T00:38:58.562Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_6c14a624-040c-4a67-8c53-754bd0be6971"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_6c14a624-040c-4a67-8c53-754bd0be6971:counts:11","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_6c14a624-040c-4a67-8c53-754bd0be6971","part":11,"quote":"**Alternative to building each connector ourselves:** a posting service with an agent connection. Examples: Postiz (open source, self-hostable, hosted plans from about $29/mo) and Ayrshare (an API, from about $149/mo).\n- **Upside:** they post through their own already-approved apps, so we skip LinkedIn's and TikTok's approval processes and the X API setup.\n- **Downside:** a per-profile cost, and a third party holds our account sign-ins."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-14T00:38:58.562Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_6c14a624-040c-4a67-8c53-754bd0be6971"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_6c14a624-040c-4a67-8c53-754bd0be6971:counts:12","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_6c14a624-040c-4a67-8c53-754bd0be6971","part":12,"quote":"## 4. With ~1,200 new bugs a day (bugs are exempt from stop-the-line), old low-severity changes and tasks never reach the top. 1,419 of the 1,805 items untouched for more than 30 days are changes or tasks."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-12T15:40:50.814Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_e58eb4b1-0c4e-42a1-97a8-a3f9bdf857c8"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_e58eb4b1-0c4e-42a1-97a8-a3f9bdf857c8:counts:5","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_e58eb4b1-0c4e-42a1-97a8-a3f9bdf857c8","part":5,"quote":"**Root cause.** One table holds three populations under one status vocabulary:\n- **work** (`nature='work'`)\n- **records** (`nature='record'`, for example 11,311 people)\n- **the signal log** (`lane='observation'`, about 235k rows)"},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-12T15:40:50.814Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_e58eb4b1-0c4e-42a1-97a8-a3f9bdf857c8"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_e58eb4b1-0c4e-42a1-97a8-a3f9bdf857c8:counts:6","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_e58eb4b1-0c4e-42a1-97a8-a3f9bdf857c8","part":6,"quote":"Records and observations carry `status='open'`, which means \"unfinished work\" everywhere else. It is not claimable, and it is exactly what the Blender picks up.\n3. **A bug** → only after a second independent reporter, or the invocation watchdog, confirms it. The bug is keyed by **signature** (tool, family, error code, field path), per D-010 of `review-system-rework-reduction-2026-09-23`."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-12T15:22:59.459Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_c2ed1456-bccc-4fc3-bd78-de566138694a"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_c2ed1456-bccc-4fc3-bd78-de566138694a:counts:8","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_c2ed1456-bccc-4fc3-bd78-de566138694a","part":8,"quote":"**What's actually wrong:** rows are still *created* per report and then *folded* afterwards. Rows filed per day were 431 / 1,739 / 2,833 / **4,067** / 3,623 / 2,289 / 1,436 / 710 (10-05 → today). 60–70% of them were closed by `system:tool-failure-signature-fold`, with a median of **10–18 minutes after creation** (11,695 folds in 7 days). The fold module's own header says nothing should mint these rows any more. The signature-keyed intake *is* in the deployed build (`d740fc3802`), so this is not the deploy freeze."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-12T15:22:59.459Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_c2ed1456-bccc-4fc3-bd78-de566138694a"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_c2ed1456-bccc-4fc3-bd78-de566138694a:counts:9","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_c2ed1456-bccc-4fc3-bd78-de566138694a","part":9,"quote":"**The fix: fold at intake.** When a capture matches an existing signature row, add to that row's occurrence count and reporter list, and attach the `tool_invocations` ids, instead of inserting a new row. The worst cases were 60 attempts over 160h (`open-source-release-2026-09-29`) and 32 attempts in 20h by a single agent (`byoc-cloud-workspaces-…`). Each attempt has a p95 of 48s.\n- 21 calls from 17 agents passed `dryRun` to `plans:set-plan-status` and were refused. Agents want a preflight.\n- An agent's memory (ef4004d3) records a **6-step serial sequence** that it had to discover one refusal at a time.\n- Precedent: `work_items:complete` had the same defect and was fixed to report every missing field in the first refusal (EI-21399023908015723). Proof freshness depends on fingerprints the caller must hand-supply\nThe ship call's `current` argument has this description: \"freshly measured evidence fingerprints… missing currentness never establishes fulfillment\". Without it, adequacy reads `unknown` and the BAR reports `bar_snapshot_proof_inadequate`. The gate's own repair text says this happens \"however good the evidence is\".\n- The background closure observer never passes fingerprints, so every orientation and portfolio read shows `proof_inadequate`. **598 BARs across 68 plans** show that code right now. Some unknown share of them is this instrument effect, not bad evidence.\n- Agents also fail on the shape (`current.N.sourceFingerprint` errors on set-plan-status).\n- **Cut:** have the gate measure current fingerprints server-side; it already knows the bound paths. This is a judgment call, because caller-supplied freshness may be deliberate. A server measurement is arguably *more* trustworthy than a transcribed one."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-11T10:21:18.030Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_c08a05b0-f7bc-4ead-872e-541b85be50c9"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_c08a05b0-f7bc-4ead-872e-541b85be50c9:counts:7","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_c08a05b0-f7bc-4ead-872e-541b85be50c9","part":7,"quote":"### 3. `plans:audit` `classRef` refusals: 72% of all audit input errors\nOf 317 input refusals, 229 come from about 130 distinct agents and are about `classRef`:\n- 166 (92 agents): \"classRef is required for activation and must be the exact prior spec-quality evaluation class\".\n- 63 (41 agents): \"classRef is activation-phase only\" (passed at completion).\n- **Cut:** derive `classRef` from the plan's prior `plans:evaluate-spec-quality` record. That is a ledger lookup, not inference from prose. Ignore it in the completion phase instead of refusing. Measured root causes"},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-10T16:13:15.251Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_8006cf99-003f-4399-9299-4f71fb0e13d8"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_8006cf99-003f-4399-9299-4f71fb0e13d8:counts:8","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_8006cf99-003f-4399-9299-4f71fb0e13d8","part":8,"quote":"### 3.1 Dead provider auth in long-lived codex processes (46 agents)\n- Every codex session's `auth.json` is a **symlink to the one shared `~/.codex/auth.json`**, which is valid now.\n- The shared login was refreshed (rotated) at **2026-10-08T00:24Z**. Codex processes started before that keep a stale in-memory refresh token. Each turn then ends with *\"Your access token could not be refreshed because you have since logged out or signed in to another account.\"*\n- Evidence: **all 46** dead sessions' codex children started before 10-08 00:24Z (latest 10-07 17:34Z); healthy ones median 10-09. Live control: **0** dead-auth.\n- The host still logs `turn-delivered` and `native-turn-start-confirmed`, so wakes *look* successful. The newest failure was 14:43Z today."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-10T16:13:15.251Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_8006cf99-003f-4399-9299-4f71fb0e13d8"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_8006cf99-003f-4399-9299-4f71fb0e13d8:counts:9","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_8006cf99-003f-4399-9299-4f71fb0e13d8","part":9,"quote":"### 3.2 Failed carry-respawn binding (57 agents, including the auditor)\n- When a codex agent self-compacts, the host relaunches codex but sometimes never captures the new session id: `respawn-carry-dropped` / `respawn-binding-unconfirmed: successor-native-id-missing`. Every later wake is short-circuited as `duplicate-delivery-id … pending` and never injected.\n- Evidence: 57 parked agents made their last tool call right at this event, against **3/87** live agents. Example su-08885e73: compacted 10-07 22:09, respawn dropped 22:12, silent for 3 days.\n- **su-c210fe1b (the auditor) died the same way.** It requested compaction at 02:28Z and made zero tool calls after; its claim was reaped at 15:47Z, about 13h later.\n- Already tracked but **blocked**: WI-10007305, WI-10002078."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-10T16:13:15.251Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_8006cf99-003f-4399-9299-4f71fb0e13d8"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_8006cf99-003f-4399-9299-4f71fb0e13d8:counts:10","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_8006cf99-003f-4399-9299-4f71fb0e13d8","part":10,"quote":"### 3.3 \"Delivered\" does not mean a turn started\n- Loop fires to stalled sessions are all recorded `status=delivered` (inbox / socket-inject / suppressed-redundant) with no turn. `coord:wake` returning \"queued\" or \"woken\" is not pickup."},"source":"report_library.body_md exact quote (not remeasured)","observedAt":"2026-11-02T03:06:44.008Z","recordedAt":"2026-10-10T16:13:15.251Z","evidenceRef":"report:rpt_8006cf99-003f-4399-9299-4f71fb0e13d8"}}},{"id":"history:report:rpt_8006cf99-003f-4399-9299-4f71fb0e13d8:counts:11","ownerId":"@audit","kind":"history","fields":{"reportedCountContext":{"status":"known","value":{"edition":"report:rpt_8006cf99-003f-4399-9299-4f71fb0e13d8","part":11,"quote":"### 3.4 The watchdog removes the last wake source\n- `stalled-loops-guard` notices \"turns-stalled\" (61 cases, e.g. 73 fires and no turn since 10-06) and **disarms the loop**. 37 of those 61 are dead-auth.\n- Its reviver (WI-37546) only revives after new tool activity, which a wedged session cannot produce. `harness/routines/reconcile-loop-routines.ts` already repairs parked schedules and missing loop-origin turns. `loop-fire.ts` reuses the shared inbox-wake executor rather than owning client-specific resume code.\n- `harness/routines/stalled-loops-guard.ts` can auto-pause a turn-stalled loop. Its revival pass requires subsequent progressing tool activity; that condition cannot help an agent unable to take its next turn.\n- `silent-halt-reconcile.ts` already has a wake-before-page rung, but its candidate population excludes armed loops. `unguarded-halt-rescue-action.ts` targets a narrower fleet/claimability case. The team already has that witness in the form of the Claude Bridge / Meridian proxy. This is the plan for turning the proxy from a routing convenience into a cryptographic source of truth for LLM-side facts. Spend-witness is the motivating use case (deferred from dogfood-v5 per its addendum 2; v5 currently ships spend as self-reported ⏱ tier-D on the Insights \"Spend\" card); the pattern is wider. Two verification traps worth carrying: (1) rank in the /api/user/search response is the RRF score carried through untouched, NOT the rerank score, so it can never be used to check rerank ordering directly; test RRF-monotonicity instead. (2) Recomputing rerank scores externally cannot settle ordering — bucketing is round(score20), so a 0.9026 lands in bucket 18 while 19 needs >=0.925, and any small text-reconstruction difference flips the bucket. Two verification traps worth carrying: (1) rank in the /api/user/search response is the RRF score carried through untouched, NOT the rerank score, so it can never be used to check rerank ordering directly; test RRF-monotonicity instead. (2) Recomputing rerank scores externally cannot settle ordering — bucketing is round(score20), so a 0.9026 lands in bucket 18 while 19 needs >=0.925, and any small text-reconstruction difference flips the bucket.
